q.s: Which Harappan site marks the western limit of the Indus Valley Civilization?
q.x: Sutkagendor on the Makran coast is the western-most Harappan site; Alamgirpur is the eastern and Manda the northern limit.

q.s: Manda, the northern-most Harappan site, is located on the bank of which river?
q.x: Manda on the Chenab (Jammu) is the northern limit and was a base for obtaining Himalayan wood; Alamgirpur lies on the Hindon.

q.s: According to the latest research, the oldest evidence of paddy cultivation in India comes from:
q.x: Lahuradeva in Uttar Pradesh has the oldest paddy; Koldihwa in the Belan valley was earlier thought to hold that distinction.

q.s: The famous 'Dancing Girl' of Mohenjodaro was made using which technique?
q.x: The bronze Dancing Girl was cast by the lost-wax (cire perdue) process.

q.s: Harappan bronze was made by alloying copper with:
q.x: Bronze is copper plus tin; copper plus zinc gives brass.

q.s: The Satavahana coins bearing a ship motif were issued by:
q.x: Ship-motif coins were issued by Yajna Sri Satakarni (and Vasishthiputra Pulumavi), pointing to maritime trade.

q.s: The Satavahana 'Karpanamulu' were coins made of:
q.x: Karpanamulu were copper coins; Satavahana coinage was mostly of lead, potin and copper.

q.s: 'Si-Yu-Ki' is the travel account of:
q.x: Hiuen Tsang wrote the Si-Yu-Ki; the Fo-Kuo-Ki is Fa-Hien's account.

q.s: The Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of:
q.x: Fa-Hien came during the reign of Chandragupta II; Hiuen Tsang came in Harsha's time.

q.s: The 'Gathasaptasati' was composed by which Satavahana king?
q.x: King Hala composed the Gathasaptasati in Maharashtri Prakrit.

q.s: Gunadhya's 'Brihatkatha' was written in which language?
q.x: Gunadhya, of the Satavahana court, wrote the Brihatkatha in Paishachi Prakrit.

q.s: All four ashramas are mentioned for the first time in the:
q.x: The Jabala Upanishad first mentions all four ashramas; the Chhandogya refers only to the first three.

q.s: The debate of Gargi and Maitreyi with Yajnavalkya is recorded in the:
q.x: The Brihadaranyaka Upanishad records Gargi and Maitreyi debating with Yajnavalkya in Janaka's court.

q.s: The statement 'The wife is half her husband' occurs in the:
q.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana calls the wife half her husband; the Maitrayani Samhita lists liquor, dice and women as three evils.

q.s: In the Rigveda, Pushan was the god of:
q.x: Pushan guarded paths, herdsmen and cattle; Aranyani was the forest goddess and Dyaus the sky.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four mathas founded by Adi Shankaracharya?
q.x: Shankara's mathas are at Sringeri, Dwaraka, Puri and Jyotirmath; Udupi is associated with Madhvacharya.

q.s: The Dhamek stupa at Sarnath marks the site of the Buddha's:
q.x: Dhamek stupa marks the first sermon (Dharmachakra-pravartana); the enlightenment took place at Bodh Gaya.

q.s: The Bharhut stupa, discovered by Alexander Cunningham in 1873, belongs to the period of the:
q.x: The Bharhut stupa is a Shunga-period monument.

q.s: Stupas that enshrine the bodily relics of the Buddha are called:
q.x: Dhatugarbha stupas such as Amaravati and Bhattiprolu hold bodily relics; Paribhogika hold objects used by the Buddha and Uddeshika are commemorative.

q.s: The idol-worshipping branch of the Svetambara Jains is known as:
q.x: The Murtipujakas worship idols; the Sthanakvasis and Terapanthis reject idol worship.

q.s: According to the Divyavadana, whom did Bindusara send to suppress the revolt at Taxila after Susima failed?
q.x: Ashoka was sent to Taxila after Susima failed; the later revolt in Ashoka's reign was handled by Kunala.

q.s: Before his accession, Ashoka served as viceroy at Taxila and:
q.x: Ashoka was viceroy at Taxila and Ujjain; Tosali lay in Kalinga, conquered only in his reign.

q.s: The Separate Kalinga Edicts of Ashoka are found at:
q.x: The Separate Kalinga Edicts are at Dhauli and Jaugada, addressed to the officers of Tosali and Samapa.

q.s: Ashoka's own account of the Kalinga war and its casualties is found in:
q.x: Rock Edict XIII describes the Kalinga war; the Separate Kalinga Edicts omit it.

q.s: The Ashokan Major Rock Edict at Erragudi is located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Erragudi is in Kurnool district.

q.s: The Ashokan edicts at Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra are written in which script?
q.x: The north-western edicts at Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra (Pakistan) are in Kharosthi.

q.s: Sri Gupta, the founder of the Gupta line, was succeeded by:
q.x: Sri Gupta was followed by Ghatotkacha, and then Chandragupta I.

q.s: Which Gupta ruler was called 'Kaviraja'?
q.x: Samudragupta, a poet and musician, was called Kaviraja.

q.s: The first Gupta ruler to assume the title 'Maharajadhiraja' was:
q.x: Chandragupta I was the first to take the title Maharajadhiraja.

q.s: Chandragupta II earned the title 'Sakari' by defeating which Western Kshatrapa ruler?
q.x: He defeated Rudrasimha III, the last Western Kshatrapa, and annexed western Malwa and Gujarat.

q.s: The Sun temple at Mandsaur was built by the guild of silk-weavers in the reign of:
q.x: The Mandsaur inscription records the silk-weavers' guild building the Sun temple under Kumaragupta I.

q.s: How many Mahapuranas are traditionally recognised?
q.x: Eighteen Mahapuranas are recognised; they took final shape in the Gupta period.

q.s: 'Kiratarjuniyam', describing Arjuna's fight with Shiva as a hunter, was written by:
q.x: Bharavi wrote Kiratarjuniyam; Magha wrote Shishupalavadha and Sriharsha Naishadhiyacharita.

q.s: Sriharsha's 'Naishadhiyacharita' deals with the story of:
q.x: Naishadhiyacharita narrates the story of Nala and Damayanti.

q.s: The 'Brihatsamhita' was written by:
q.x: Varahamihira wrote the Brihatsamhita; Aryabhatta wrote the Aryabhatiya.

q.s: Under the Cholas, the assembly of the nadu, a group of villages, was known as the:
q.x: The nattar of the nadu handled revenue and disputes above the village; ur and sabha were village assemblies and nagaram the merchants' body.

q.s: The 'Dar-ul-Shifa' established by Firoz Shah Tughlaq was a:
q.x: Dar-ul-Shifa was a free hospital; Diwan-i-Khairat handled charity.

q.s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq's 'Diwan-i-Bandagan' was a department of:
q.x: Diwan-i-Bandagan looked after slaves, said to number about 1,80,000.

q.s: The 'Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi' was written by:
q.x: Yahiya bin Ahmad Sarhindi wrote it in the reign of the Sayyid Sultan Mubarak Shah.

q.s: Who founded the Sayyid dynasty of Delhi?
q.x: Khizr Khan founded the Sayyid dynasty in 1414, ruling as deputy of Timur's son Shah Rukh.

q.s: 'Gulrukhi' was the pen-name of which Sultan of Delhi?
q.x: Sikandar Lodi wrote Persian verse under the pen-name Gulrukhi; Alauddin Khalji styled himself Sikandar-i-Sani.

q.s: Which Sultan of Delhi was called 'Lakh Baksh' for his generosity?
q.x: Qutbuddin Aibak, who ruled as Malik, was called Lakh Baksh.

q.s: Balban's title 'Zil-i-Ilahi' means:
q.x: Zil-i-Ilahi means 'Shadow of God'; Niyabat-i-Khudai (Deputy of God) was another of his titles.

q.s: Which dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate had the shortest rule?
q.x: The Khalji dynasty lasted only about 30 years (1290-1320).

q.s: Gulbadan Begum wrote the 'Humayun-nama' at the request of:
q.x: Gulbadan Begum, Humayun's sister, wrote the Humayun-nama at Akbar's request.

q.s: Babur's memoir 'Tuzuk-i-Baburi' was written in:
q.x: Babur wrote his memoirs in Turki; they were later translated into Persian.

q.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Adina Mosque is at Pandua in Bengal, not Gujarat.

q.s: Who built the second, third and fourth storeys of the Qutb Minar?
q.x: Aibak built the first storey (c. 1199); Iltutmish added the next three.

q.s: The fifth storey of the Qutb Minar was added by:
q.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq added the fifth storey; the minar is about 72.5 m high.

q.s: The Telugu work 'Basava Puranam' was written by:
q.x: Palkuriki Somanatha wrote the Basava Puranam; Srinatha wrote Kasi Khandam.

q.s: 'Ranganatha Ramayanam' was composed by:
q.x: Gona Budda Reddy wrote the Ranganatha Ramayanam; Tikkana wrote the Nirvachanottara Ramayanam.

q.s: Akbar's last military campaign ended with the capture of:
q.x: Asirgarh in Khandesh, taken in 1601, was Akbar's last conquest.

q.s: Who defended Ahmednagar against the Mughal forces of Akbar?
q.x: Chand Bibi resisted the Mughal attack on Ahmednagar.

q.s: Itimad-ud-Daulah (Ghiyas Beg), the father of Nur Jahan, served as diwan under:
q.x: Ghiyas Beg was Jahangir's diwan; Sa'adullah Khan served Shah Jahan.

q.s: Sa'adullah Khan was the diwan of which Mughal emperor?
q.x: Sa'adullah Khan was Shah Jahan's diwan; Asad Khan served Aurangzeb.

q.s: The 'Razmnama', the Persian translation of the Mahabharata, was produced by:
q.x: The Razmnama was prepared by Akbar's translation bureau, the Maktab Khana.

q.s: Vedanta Desika was the leader of which sub-sect of Sri Vaishnavism?
q.x: Vedanta Desika led the Vadakalai; both Vadakalai and Tengalai follow Vishishtadvaita.

q.s: Gaudiya Vaishnavism was founded by:
q.x: Chaitanya founded Gaudiya Vaishnavism; Madhva's Brahma Sampradaya is centred at Udupi.

q.s: The Pushtimarga, which worships child Krishna as Shrinathji, was founded by:
q.x: Vallabhacharya founded the Pushtimarga; Nimbarka taught Dvaitadvaita with Radha-Krishna worship.

q.s: The Vellore mutiny took place in the year:
q.x: The Vellore mutiny of 1806 was provoked by a new dress code and a ban on caste marks.

q.s: The Revolt of 1857 broke out at Meerut on:
q.x: The Meerut rising began on 10 May 1857; 29 March 1857 was Mangal Pandey's action at Barrackpore.

q.s: Who suppressed the Revolt of 1857 at Jhansi and Gwalior?
q.x: Hugh Rose defeated Rani Lakshmibai at Jhansi and Gwalior; Nicholson fell in the assault on Delhi.

q.s: The Revolt of 1857 in Bihar was led by:
q.x: Kunwar Singh of Jagdishpur led the revolt in Bihar; Liyakat Ali led at Allahabad.

q.s: Who described the Revolt of 1857 as 'a mere sepoy mutiny'?
q.x: J.R. Seeley called it a mere sepoy mutiny; T.R. Holmes saw a conflict of civilisation and barbarism.

q.s: The Revolt of 1857 was described as 'a conflict between civilisation and barbarism' by:
q.x: T.R. Holmes; L.E.R. Rees called it a war of fanatic religionists against Christians.

q.s: The Battle of St. Thome (Adyar), 1746, was fought during the:
q.x: At St. Thome in 1746 about 930 French troops defeated some 10,000 of the Nawab's men.

q.s: The First Carnatic War came to an end with the Treaty of:
q.x: The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) ended it and restored the pre-war position, including Madras to the English.

q.s: Kandregula Jogipantulu, who helped the British secure the Northern Circars, was made Majumdar of which place by Nizam Ali?
q.x: Nizam Ali made him Majumdar of Rajamahendravaram; the British gave him the title Raja Bahadur.

q.s: The Treaty of Lahore (1846), which ended the First Anglo-Sikh War, was concluded during the tenure of:
q.x: The Treaty of Lahore was signed under Hardinge I.

q.s: The Public Works Department was set up by:
q.x: Dalhousie created the Public Works Department.

q.s: The policy of 'Masterly Inactivity' towards Afghanistan is associated with:
q.x: Sir John Lawrence (1864-69) followed non-interference in Afghanistan; the Bhutan (Duar) War was also fought in his time.

q.s: Who became the first Law Member of the Governor-General's Council under the Charter Act of 1833?
q.x: Macaulay was added as the fourth (Law) Member; the post is the origin of the Ministry of Law and Justice.

q.s: The First Law Commission under Macaulay to codify Indian laws was set up in:
q.x: The First Law Commission was set up in 1834.

q.s: In the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), Phase 5 denotes:
q.x: The IPC has five phases: Minimal, Stressed, Crisis, Emergency and Catastrophe/Famine.

q.s: The Simla Deputation that met Lord Minto on 1 October 1906 was led by:
q.x: Aga Khan III led the deputation seeking weightage for Muslims.

q.s: The Lucknow Pact between the Congress and the Muslim League was signed in:
q.x: Muslim League 1906, Morley-Minto Reforms 1909, Lucknow Pact 1916, Jallianwala Bagh 1919.

q.s: The Harijan temple entry at Siddhantam on 17 December 1933 took place during the Andhra tour of:
q.x: It occurred during Gandhi's Harijan tour of Andhra, when he collected Harijana Bhiksha.

q.s: The Sati Regulation (XVII of 1829) was passed under:
q.x: William Bentinck abolished sati in 1829.

q.s: The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act was passed in:
q.x: The 1856 Act legalised widow remarriage and made children of such marriages legitimate.

q.s: The Depressed Classes Mission (1906) was founded by:
q.x: V.R. Shinde founded the Depressed Classes Mission on 18 October 1906.

q.s: B.R. Ambedkar founded the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha in:
q.x: The Sabha (1924) used the slogan 'Educate, Agitate, Organise'; the Independent Labour Party came in 1936.

q.s: Gandhi's Harijan tour of November 1933 - July 1934 began from:
q.x: The tour of about 20,000 km started from Wardha.

q.s: The Wardha Scheme of Basic Education was drawn up by a committee headed by:
q.x: The Zakir Hussain Committee's scheme was adopted at Haripura in 1938.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Wardha Scheme of Basic Education?
o: Free and compulsory education for seven years
Mother tongue as the medium of instruction
English as the medium of instruction
q.x: The scheme used the mother tongue, not English, as the medium.

q.s: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Scientific Society in:
q.x: The Scientific Society was founded in 1864 at Ghazipur; the MAO College came in 1875.

q.s: The Indian League (1875) was founded by:
q.x: Sisir Kumar Ghosh founded the Indian League; Dwarkanath Tagore was a founder of the Landholders' Society.

q.s: The Bombay Association (1852) was founded by:
q.x: Jagannath Shankar Sheth founded the Bombay Association.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Dadabhai Naoroji is correct?
o: He presided over the Indian National Congress four times.
He raised Swaraj as the national demand at the Surat session of 1907.
He said that Britain was 'bleeding India white'.
He presided over the Madras session of 1893.
q.x: Naoroji, author of the drain theory, said Britain was bleeding India white; he presided three times (1886, 1893 Lahore, 1906), raising Swaraj at Calcutta 1906.

q.s: At which Congress session did Dadabhai Naoroji declare Swaraj to be the national goal?
q.x: He announced Swaraj as the goal at the Calcutta session of 1906.

q.s: The Chittagong Armoury Raid of April 1930 was led by:
q.x: Surya Sen, Secretary of the Chittagong District Congress Committee, led the raid under the Indian Republican Army.

q.s: Surya Sen was hanged by the British in:
q.x: Surya Sen was hanged in 1934.

q.s: The 'Tinkathia' system of indigo cultivation was associated with:
q.x: Tinkathia (indigo on 3/20 of the land) was the grievance in Champaran (1917), ended by the Champaran Agrarian Act, 1918.

q.s: The Pabna agrarian movement led to the passing of the:
q.x: Pabna led to the Bengal Tenancy Act; the Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act followed the Deccan riots.

q.s: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 was popularly described as:
o: No Vakil, No Dalil, No Appeal
q.x: The Act, based on the Sedition Committee report of Justice Sidney Rowlatt, allowed detention without trial.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT part of the Non-Cooperation programme of 1920?
o: Promotion of khadi and the charkha
q.x: Breaking the salt law belongs to the Civil Disobedience Movement of 1930.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a proposal of the Cripps Mission (1942)?
o: Dominion status for an Indian Union after the war
A constitution-making body to be set up after the war
An option for unwilling provinces to stay outside the Union
Immediate transfer of defence to Indian hands
q.x: Defence was to remain with the British during the war; the other three were Cripps proposals.

q.s: The first Indian National Army (1942) was organised by:
q.x: Captain Mohan Singh raised the first INA; it was dissolved in December 1942 after he quarrelled with the Japanese.

q.s: The Bangkok Conference of June 1942 placed the INA under the:
q.x: The Bangkok Conference placed the INA under the Indian Independence League.

q.s: Subhas Chandra Bose raised the Free Indian Legion from Indian prisoners of war in:
q.x: The Legion was raised in Germany from Indian POWs captured by Germany and Italy in North Africa; Azad Hind Radio also began in Germany.

q.s: The Bal Charkha Sangh was founded by:
q.x: Indira Gandhi founded the Bal Charkha Sangh and the Vanar Sena.

q.s: The Nationalist Party of 1934 was formed by:
q.x: Malaviya formed the Nationalist Party in 1934; Nehru and Bose formed the Independence for India League in 1928.

q.s: Gandhi's Gujarati work 'Sarvodaya' is a rendering of:
o: Tolstoy's 'The Kingdom of God is Within You'
q.x: Sarvodaya renders Ruskin's Unto This Last; Hind Swaraj (1909) is Gandhi's own original work.

q.s: Who was the constitutional adviser of the Nizam during the integration of Hyderabad?
q.x: Sir Walter Monckton advised the Nizam; Sidney Cotton was the Australian pilot who ran arms into Hyderabad.

q.s: 'Operation Polo' (1948) was related to the integration of:
q.x: Operation Polo, under J.N. Chaudhuri, ended the Nizam's resistance in September 1948.

q.s: 'Operation Meghdoot' (1984) was carried out in:
q.x: Operation Meghdoot secured the Siachen glacier; Blue Star was at the Golden Temple and Vijay in Goa.

q.s: Who presided over the first Andhra Mahasabha held at Bapatla in 1913?
q.x: B.N. Sarma presided at Bapatla; Nyapati Subba Rao presided over the second session.

q.s: The 'Andhra Patrika' (1908) was started by:
q.x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded Andhra Patrika; Krishna Patrika was associated with Konda Venkatappayya.

q.s: Under the Nizam's Mulki rules, besides birth, a person could become a Mulki by continuous residence in Hyderabad State for:
q.x: Fifteen years' continuous residence made a person a Mulki.

q.s: The Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act was passed in:
q.x: Parliament passed the Act in 1957.

q.s: The Girglani Commission (2001) examined:
o: Violations of GO 610 and the 1975 Presidential Order
Formation of the Telangana Regional Committee
q.x: Girglani examined GO 610 violations; the 1969 Bhargava Committee looked into Telangana's revenue surpluses.

q.s: Under the 1969 Eight-Point Formula, the Bhargava Committee examined:
q.x: Justice Vashist Bhargava's committee assessed Telangana's revenue surpluses; Wanchoo gave legal opinion on job safeguards.

q.s: Himachal Pradesh became a full-fledged State in:
q.x: Himachal Pradesh was a Union Territory under the 1956 Act and became a State in 1971.

q.s: Nagaland became a State of the Indian Union in:
q.x: Nagaland was formed in 1963; Gujarat was formed in 1960.

q.s: The oldest stupa in Andhra Pradesh, with relic caskets of the 3rd century BC, is at:
q.x: Bhattiprolu's relic caskets belong to the oldest stupa in AP; its inscriptions are in Prakrit in a local variant of Brahmi.

q.s: The Kali era began in:
q.x: The Kali era starts in 3102 BC; the Kalachuri/Chedi era in 248 AD.

q.s: The Harsha era began in:
q.x: The Harsha era dates from his accession in 606 AD; 319 AD is the Gupta era.

q.s: The sculptures of the Amaravati school were made of:
q.x: Amaravati used white Palnadu limestone; Gandhara used grey-blue schist and Mathura spotted red sandstone.

q.s: The Gandhara school of art mainly used:
q.x: Gandhara sculptures are in grey-blue schist.

q.s: The Bhagavata religion entered Andhra under which Satavahana king?
q.x: It came into Andhra under Kanha, the second Satavahana king.

q.s: According to the Chhandogya Upanishad, the teacher of Krishna was:
q.x: The Chhandogya Upanishad names Ghora Angirasa as Krishna's teacher.

q.s: Ayaka platforms, with five pillars in each of the four directions, are a feature of:
q.x: Ayaka platforms belong to Buddhist stupas such as those of Nagarjunakonda and Amaravati.

q.s: The Telugu grammar 'Andhra Shabda Chintamani' was written by:
q.x: Nannaya, the Adikavi, wrote it and bore the title Shabda Shasanudu.

q.s: Nannaya was the court poet of the Eastern Chalukya king:
q.x: Nannaya translated the Mahabharata at the court of Rajaraja Narendra.

q.s: Which Chola king was killed in the battle of Koppam (1053) against Someshvara I?
q.x: Rajadhiraja I fell at Koppam; the Chola-Chalukya wars arose over Vengi and the Raichur doab.

q.s: The battle of Kudalasangamam (c. 1062) was fought at the confluence of:
q.x: Kudalasangamam lies at the Krishna-Tungabhadra confluence, where the Cholas defeated Someshvara I.

q.s: Which Nellore Choda ruler took the title 'Chola Sthapanacharya' after placing Rajendra Chola on the Chola throne?
q.x: Tikkana Choda (Tikka I) restored Rajendra Chola and took the title.

q.s: 'Sringara Naishadham', on the story of Nala and Damayanti, was written by:
q.x: Srinatha wrote Sringara Naishadham and Kashikhandam.

q.s: 'Veerabhadra Vijayam' was written by:
q.x: Veerabhadra Vijayam is a work of Bammera Potana.

q.s: The victories of Kayastha Ambadeva against Rudrama Devi are recorded in which inscription?
q.x: The Tripurantakam inscription records Ambadeva's victories.

q.s: The death of Rani Rudrama Devi is recorded in which inscription?
q.x: The Chandupatla inscription records Rudrama Devi's death.

q.s: Which Kondavidu Reddi ruler succeeded Anavema Reddi in 1386?
q.x: Anavema ruled 1364-1386, Kumaragiri 1386-1402, Pedakomati Vema 1402-1420 and Racha Vema 1420-1424.

q.s: Anitalli, who issued the Kaluvacheru inscription, was the daughter of:
q.x: Anitalli, daughter of Kataya Vema and wife of Veerabhadra Reddi, issued it after Rajahmundry was recaptured in 1423.

q.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler backed Kataya Vema against Kondavidu?
q.x: Deva Raya I supported Kataya Vema of Rajahmundry against Kondavidu.

q.s: In the Reddi village administration, the village accountant was the:
q.x: The Karnam kept the accounts; the village had 12 Ayagars paid in Manyam land or Mera.

q.s: Krishnadevaraya's 'Amuktamalyada' is also known as:
q.x: Amuktamalyada is also called Vishnuchittiyam.

q.s: The title 'Amuktamalyada' refers to:
q.x: It refers to the heroine Andal, who offered the garland she had worn; it is the first Telugu work named after its heroine.

q.s: Which foreign traveller compared the city of Vijayanagara to Rome?
q.x: Domingo Paes said the city was as large as Rome; Abdur Razzaq spoke of 300 ports, each equal to Calicut.

q.s: A temple with three shrines on one plan, such as the Thousand Pillar temple at Hanamkonda, is called a:
q.x: A trikutalaya has three shrines on a common plan.

q.s: Under the Permanent Settlement, the zamindars kept what share of the revenue collected?
q.x: Zamindars kept one-eleventh and paid ten-elevenths to the government.

q.s: The Permanent Settlement was applied to the Andhra region in:
q.x: Introduced by Cornwallis in Bengal in 1793, it came to Andhra in 1802.

q.s: The name 'Rayalaseema' was adopted at the Andhra Mahasabha held at Nandyal in 1928 on the proposal of:
q.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao proposed the name at Nandyal in November 1928.

q.s: 'Andhra Prakasika' (1885), the first political journal in Andhra, was edited by:
q.x: A.P. Parthasarathi Naidu edited Andhra Prakasika from Madras; Nyapathi Subbarao brought out Vyjayanti.

q.s: 'Krishna Patrika' was started at Machilipatnam in 1902 by:
q.x: Konda Venkatappayya started it with Dasu Narayana Rao; Mutnuri Krishna Rao was its later editor.

q.s: Which of the following was a founder of the Hyderabad State Comrades Association (1939)?
q.x: Makhdoom Mohiuddin founded it with Raj Bahadur Gour and Syed Ibrahim; it mobilised peasants for the Telangana armed struggle.

q.s: The song 'Desamunu preminchumanna' (Desamante matti kadoi, desamante manushuloi) was written by:
q.x: It is from Gurajada Apparao's Mutyala Saralu (1910).

q.s: India's national pledge 'Bharata Desam Naa Matrubhoomi' was written by:
q.x: Paidimarri Venkata Subbarao wrote the pledge.

q.s: Sri Sri's 'Mahaprasthanam' was published in:
q.x: Its poems were written between 1933 (Jayabheri) and 1947; the collection was published in 1950.

q.s: Who was elected the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 December 1946?
q.x: Rajendra Prasad became permanent President; Sachchidananda Sinha was the temporary President.

q.s: Who among the following was a Vice-President of the Constituent Assembly?
